limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Detect exposed host overhead and diagnose per-step host regressions in CUDA inference serving from existing nsys timelines.
applicability.prerequisites: An existing serving nsys trace and Python with sqlite3; comparative root-cause analysis needs baseline and target traces, with nsys export available for report-format input.
applicability.input_contract: One trace for detection/breakdown or two comparable traces for regression analysis, including the workload/phase context needed to isolate steady-state forward steps.
applicability.produced_artifact: A detection verdict with metric/phase evidence, per-step NVTX/kernel/API breakdown and ranked host-operation deltas for a targeted optimization handoff.
applicability.failure_modes: Warmup/loading or mismatched phase mixtures distort per-step comparisons; duplicated rank ranges, unresolved NVTX text IDs or overlapping rank end times can miscompute host gaps.

recommendations: Isolate comparable steady-state forward iterations and inspect context/generation separately; aggregate utilization can hide a phase-specific host bottleneck.
Confirm exposed preparation using both performance impact and idle attribution, retain communication as a confounder, and triage absolute NVTX time deltas before line-level optimization.
Resolve NVTX text IDs, account for TP rank duplication and use the maximum overlapping end time for gaps; do not compare full-trace totals as per-step overhead.
